evidence_quote: Whereas the identification of two intronic mutations in ABCA1, located on opposite chromosomes may have predicted the Tangier Disease phenotype, the patient did not exhibit any of the known clinical features of this disorder
note: Close call: proband and sister carry two ABCA1 splice variants (HDL 12 and 22 mg/dL) but are presented as hypoalphalipoproteinemia, not Tangier disease; included under the two-variants rule.

evidence_quote: Tangier disease was described by Fredrickson and colleagues in 1961 in two young siblings from Tangier Island in the Chesapeake Bay.
note: Narrative review; Tangier patients appear only as the historical siblings and in figure legends not stated to be new; the individual-level cases (APOA1) are another disease.

evidence_quote: DNA analysis has revealed a new mutation (C2033A) in both alleles, causing a premature stop codon at the amino acid residue 573, which resulted in truncation of the ABCA1 protein [18].
note: Patient previously described by Kolovou et al.

evidence_quote: There were four homozygous subjects for the ABCA1 variant two of which were also heterozygous for the LPL variant
note: Close call: four S1731C homozygotes in a low HDL-C family (HDL-C about 0.95 mmol/L) are never called Tangier disease; the paper treats low HDL-C as a complex trait.

evidence_quote: Molecular analysis of ABCA1 gene showed the presence of a novel homozygous deletion (c.4464-486_4698 + 382 Del).
A diagnosis of Tangier disease was ascertained.
note: Diagnosis by lipid profile and biopsies; genetic testing not done. Probably the same patient as 27011649.

evidence_quote: The combination of facial diplegia and predominant involvement of upper limbs is the characteristic clinical phenotype; this coupled with the typical lipid profile and nerve biopsy observations clinched the diagnosis of Tangier disease.
note: No genetic testing; probably the same patient as 26713019.

evidence_quote: We have again recently reviewed this relationship in our own cases and those in the literature (total of 185 cases).
note: Narrative review; Tangier cases only in aggregate or the historical Fredrickson siblings; individual patients described are APOA1 or LCAT disease.

evidence_quote: The resequencing of ABCA1 in the proband evidenced the mutation c.5094C > A p.Tyr1698* (legacy name Y1698X) (Figure 2B).
note: One Italian family; three homozygotes (AC, DC, RC) counted, heterozygous sister CC not counted.

evidence_quote: In terms of ABCA1 gene mutation, this patient had compound heterozygosity for V825I and N935T.
note: Own patient plus a per-patient Table 1 of 132 earlier cases (133 total, as in the text); only the new patient has genotype in the table-free text.

evidence_quote: Patient 1 had a heterozygous deletion spanning exon 4; Patient 2 and Patient 3, a pair of siblings, had a heterozygous deletion spanning exons 8 to 31; and Patient 4 had a heterozygous deletion spanning the entire ABCA1 gene.
note: Four heterozygous ABCA1 deletion carriers with hypoalphalipoproteinemia; no Tangier patient in the paper.

evidence_quote: Based on the above results, we diagnosed the patient with a genetic Tangier disease.
note: Close call: a single heterozygous ABCA1 variant (c.598G>A, inherited from the mother) but the authors diagnose Tangier disease; abstract miswrites the gene as ABCD1.
